13. **Command at a distance.** Distance inside the realm (every order a king gives inside his realm travels from where he is, levies included, carried by the realm's own couriers; "Distance inside your own realm"), the capital where the king is, commanders whose competence sets their tactical search, army mandates, "No commander, no mandate", and governors who raise levies and collect yield under a mandate ("Governors") ("Command at a distance" and "Ruling by mandate" in the Ideas tab; question 7 of the old round report). Depends on items 7 and 10. Armies march by item 7's measure of distance too ("Distance-based marching"), and in the pace rule this item turns on an army's size and forced marches ("What sets a company's pace"). Standing orders become part of a commander's mandate ("Standing orders belong to commanders" in the Ideas tab): a standing order is carried out by the commander with the army, or by the king if he is there; it comes into force only when it has reached the army, travelling like any order inside the realm; it fires on what that army can see, not on all the king sees; and the commander's loyalty and competence shape how he carries it out. An army with no commander present does not react, but it follows plain orders to the letter: move, hold, attack and support as told, when the order reaches it, and scheduled orders as written, with no standing orders and no adapting; meeting an enemy, it fights as combat says ("No commander, no mandate"). Until this item, standing orders work as the fix pass built them. Scheduled and conditional orders read only what is known where they run ("Scheduled, conditional orders" under Pacing). A commander also decides how a hungry army takes its food: a good one in order, doing less harm, a poor or disloyal one by looting ("Armies need food as well as pay" in the Ideas tab). A fallen kingdom's army with no commander may raise a captain from its own ranks instead of disbanding, while an army that is paid and fed never does ("A kingdom falls with its capital" in this tab; "A head rises where men lack one" in the Ideas tab). A king may also go in person, to lead an army, carry his own letter or visit a foreign court, by the same rules of travel and interception ("The capital is wherever the king is" in the Ideas tab); what he sees as current is whatever a courier could bring him within the season, and the map can draw that reach around him ("Distance inside your own realm"). **Stop for review.**
